collector_notes: Pool arithmetic: results/expA/candidates.json is expected to yield 13 matrix rows in 12 families. These 19 candidates add 16 architecture families that are new to the pool (edgenext, tinyvit, xcit, rtdetr, inception_v3, mnasnet, squeezenet, retinaface, movenet, yolox, semantic_fpn, mobilenet_v1, deeplab_v3, inception_v1, yolov4_tiny, yolo_fastest), 5 publishers new to the pool (CoreEpoch, Arm, AMD, the 'onnx' HF organisation, Thefalley) and at least 4 export toolchains new to the pool (Kenosis, PyTorch PT2E, onnxruntime quantize_static/QOperator, TFLite-to-ONNX static QDQ).

A11 / P5: the paper may use the word 'independent' of Arm 1's quantizers only if the flagged set F carries at least two distinct export_tooling values. Before this round every non-onnx/models candidate came from transformers.js. b17/b18/b19 (onnxruntime quantize_static) and b05 (PT2E) are the two named, reproducible non-transformers.js toolchains most likely to clear that bar; b01-b04 (Kenosis) add a third, proprietary one.

Per-publisher caps (A9a, 6 per publisher) as this list stands: CoreEpoch 4, AMD 6 (at cap; two further AMD files are held in known_rejections as reserves), Thefalley 3, ketiswp 3 here plus a16 already in A's list = 4, Arm 2, 'onnx' HF organisation 1. No publisher exceeds 6, but ketiswp must be counted across both lists.

Positive-class coverage, stated as a weakness rather than hidden: the families most likely to carry a two-element-block single-axis Transpose in 8 bits are b01 edgenext, b02 tinyvit, b03 xcit and b04/b06 rtdetr. Four of those five come from one publisher (CoreEpoch) and one toolchain (Kenosis). The collector could not find a second publisher of static-INT8 ONNX vision transformers under 60 MB anywhere on the hub.

L4 method: 'gated' was read from the hub API for every repository (all false) AND every URL above was fetched with an anonymous HTTP HEAD that returned 200 with a Content-Length - no login, no gate, no click-through, no terms dialog. No repository in this list required accepting anything.

What was looked for and NOT found, so the next collector does not repeat it: EfficientFormer, LeViT, PoolFormer, RepViT, FastViT, EdgeNeXt (outside b01), SegFormer, MobileOne, EfficientViT, NextViT, SwiftFormer and CoaT exist on the hub only as FP32 ONNX (onnxmodelzoo/*_Opset16/17/18, Xenova timm exports) or in non-ONNX NPU formats (mobilint/*); no third party publishes them as 8-bit ONNX under 60 MB. Swin from a publisher other than Xenova exists only as ExecuTorch/LiteRT (Arm) or above the size cap (onnx-community/swin-finetuned-food101, already rejected in A). OpenVINO publishes IR (.xml/.bin), not ONNX; its HF organisation has zero ONNX models. No MobileViT export was proposed, as instructed.
Nothing was downloaded. The only bytes fetched were model cards, config.json / config.yaml / metadata.yaml / quantize_config.json files, inference and quantization scripts, and HTTP HEAD responses.
